title: 포기는 빠른 편이라  (I Tend to Give Up Quickly)

segments.t: Outside his home, rookie producer Baek Seung-chan runs into Shin Hye-joo, the senior he has a crush on. She casually mentions her boyfriend, breaking his heart. Listen for "namchin", slang for boyfriend, and "pogi", meaning 'giving up'.
제가 아니다 싶으면 포기는 빠른 편이라.
솔직히 아까 오후에 봤을 때는 놀랐죠.
Let's unpack those twelve lines one turn at a time.
'Your house is here?' Hye-joo recognizes him and asks a quick question using "jibi", 'house', and "yeogi", 'here'.
'Do you live here too, noona?' Seung-chan answers with his own polite question. He calls her "nuna", a respectful term for an older female friend, and asks "saseyo", 'do you live'.
'No, not me, my boyfriend.' Hye-joo casually drops a bomb. She says "na malgo", 'not me', and introduces "nae namchin", short for 'my boyfriend'.
'He is doing 2 Days and 1 Night right now.' She mentions his show using "jigeum", 'right now'. The ending "hageodeun" explains what he does in a friendly tone.
'By the way, where did you get assigned?' Hye-joo changes the subject with "cham", 'by the way'. She asks about his "baejeong", 'assignment', with "eodiro", 'to where'.
'It hasn't come out yet.' Seung-chan formally replies using "ajik", 'yet', and the negative adverb "an". He finishes with "natseumnida", the polite form of 'came out'.
'Really? Come on over. I am there.' Hye-joo invites him using "geurae", 'really', and the command "wa", 'come'. She adds "na geogi itjana", 'you know I am there'.
제가 아니다 싶으면 포기는 빠른 편이라.

'I tend to give up quickly if I think it's not meant to be.' Seung-chan tries to save face. He uses "pogi", 'giving up', and "ppareun pyeonira", meaning 'tend to be fast'. He prefaces this with "anida sipeumyeon", 'if I think it is not'.
솔직히 아까 오후에 봤을 때는 놀랐죠.
'Honestly, I was surprised when I saw you this afternoon.' Seung-chan admits his feelings using "soljiki", 'honestly', and "ohue", 'in the afternoon'. He confesses he was "nollatjyo", 'surprised'.
'Because I am human too.' He justifies his reaction using "jeodo", 'me too', and "saraminikka", 'because I am a person'.
'But now I am really totally fine,' Seung-chan lies bravely. He uses "geunde jigeumeun", 'but now', and "jeongmal", 'really'. The phrase "amureochido anko" means 'not bothered at all'.

'I hope the two of you have a beautiful love.' Seung-chan delivers a painful blessing. He uses "du bun", 'you two', and "yeppeun saranghasyeosseumyeon", 'wish you have a beautiful love', ending with "jokesseoyo", 'I hope'. Now let's listen to the whole awkward encounter again.
제가 아니다 싶으면 포기는 빠른 편이라.
솔직히 아까 오후에 봤을 때는 놀랐죠.
From "namchin" for boyfriend to "baejeong" for assignment, you now have the vocabulary for workplace gossip and romance. Keep practicing!
